current_answer:
As of 30 October 2026, public evidence does not establish broad capability decline across popular AI models. AI Stupid Level’s 30 October page snapshot reports no below-baseline result among 25 models on its API-side 24-hour boards; none of 66 armed model-suite detectors fired, while nine remain unarmed. Claude Opus 5.5’s latest 10-day LiveNerf window is labeled ‘no change’: its score is 0.571 ± 0.035, with a baseline delta of −0.015 ± 0.018 over 78 items. These monitors test selected routes and tasks, not every consumer surface or a reader’s own workflow.

OpenAI’s release notes on 29 October canceled the planned Pro 200 reduction in Work and Codex usage. Pro 200 users on the lower allowance received twice their previous allowance, matching users who already had the higher amount; Pro 100 and Pro 500 Work/Codex allowances also doubled. OpenAI says Pro 200 remains $200/month. Allowance is not a fixed number of messages or tasks, so check Settings → Usage before reacting to the older notice. OpenAI separately marked a GPT-6.1 Sol API performance incident resolved on 27 October. ABIS flagged a possible Gemini 3.5 Flash version change on 27 October, with a change in its behavior-drift measure; that is not evidence of a capability decline. Recent ChatGPT complaints focus on conversational tone and continuity, but they are not matched task tests.

catalogue_card.question: Did OpenAI cut Pro 200 usage today—and are models getting worse?
catalogue_card.text: The planned Work/Codex reduction was canceled on 29 October; lower-allowance Pro 200 users received twice their former allowance. Current public tests do not establish broad model decline, though they show a resolved GPT-6.1 Sol API event and a Gemini behavior-change signal.

summary: Broad capability decline across popular AI models is not established as of 30 October 2026.

AI Stupid Level’s page snapshot dated 30 October, 03:26 UTC reports no below-baseline score among 25 models on its API-side 24-hour boards; zero of 66 armed detectors fired, while nine remain unarmed.
LiveNerf labels its 21–30-day Claude Opus 5.5 window “no change”: −0.015 ± 0.018 from its baseline over 78 calibrated items; this is one pinned Claude Code subscription path.
ABIS labels a 27 October Gemini 3.5 Flash behavior-drift signal a possible version update; its metric moved, but the result does not establish a capability decline.
OpenAI’s status record says a GPT-6.1 Sol API performance event affecting Chat Completions, Responses, and Batch was resolved on 27 October.

OpenAI canceled the planned Pro 200 Work/Codex allowance reduction on 29 October; lower-allowance accounts received twice their prior allowance to match higher accounts. Pro 100 and Pro 500 Work/Codex allowances also doubled.
Community reports describe conversational-tone and continuity concerns alongside positive experiences. They are not matched task tests or a representative sample.
Check your current plan allowance and status first; compare a safe, repeated task only after fixing the product surface, model selection, effort, and context.
uncertainty: AI Stupid Level reports its own API-side results and does not publish the underlying task set; nine of 75 model-suite detectors are not yet armed.
LiveNerf measures Claude Opus 5.5 through a pinned Claude Code subscription path on its calibrated panel; it does not establish how consumer Claude or another task performs.
ABIS labels the Gemini 3.5 Flash event a possible version update signal. Its behavior-drift metric does not by itself say capability improved or declined.
OpenAI status confirms its declared GPT-6.1 Sol API performance event and resolution, not root cause, affected-account outcome, or a model-weight change.
Community reports are self-selected and lack matched task artifacts, verified serving receipts, and a representative denominator.
Actual allowance depends on plan, model, task, and settings; the OpenAI help page directs users to Settings → Usage for their account-specific values.
First-party pool analytics were unavailable; reach, return use, switching, sharing, follows, and funding remain unknown.
